result:
**STOP — B needs to rule on A-R237-REVIEW-M1 (Medium) before this round can hand over.** The planned work is applied and green, but it introduces a regression whose fix is outside my grants (lesson L33).

**The regression:** a refusal like "Undo/Redo does not work while dragging" can be showing when the demo collection finishes loading. The new settle rule keeps that refusal on screen. When the gesture ends, the provider puts back the last non-refusal status, which is still `Loading the demo collection…`, and nothing clears it after that. At HEAD this didn't happen, because the plain "ready" write replaced the refusal.
- **Unit proof:** a TU12-shaped test, run on scratch copies outside the repo, fails on this round's tree (shows `Loading…`) and passes on HEAD `ecaf0e4`. Logs: `a-round-237/tu12-fixed-tree.log` and `tu12-head.log`.
- **Browser proof:** reproduced in Chromium on :5173 at both 1440×900 and 1280×720. With the MP3s delayed, I held a Volume fader, pressed Ctrl+Z, waited until loading had finished (the hero row already showed its 02:30.372 duration), then released. The final status was `Loading the demo collection…`. Evidence is in `refusal-probe.json` and the two screenshots.
- **Candidate fix (not applied to the repo):** one extra line in `settle` that updates `lastNonRefusalStatusRef`, plus a TU12 row. It's in `a-round-237/candidate-fix.diff`. On scratch, TU12 passed, and so did 5 status/collection test files (54 tests) and 23 refusal-related files (492 tests). That is not the full covering set. It does not fix the reviewer's L1 (Low, same cause: if the seed fires during a drag, "refusal + seed" stays on screen), so L1 needs its own decision.

**What's in the tree:** B's pre-checked diff, applied unchanged, plus the three doc changes (docs 182, 183 and the new 185). It's exactly the 9 granted files plus the 2 new ones. The frozen and root-file hashes still match, and no protected file was touched.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Typecheck | passes |
| Biome on the 8 changed code/test files | clean |
| Covering tests (121 files) | 1,715 passed. Nothing above 50 % of its timeout; slowest is CP12 at 6.6 s of 30 s at gate 236 |
| Mutants | MU-RC fails TU9 and TU10; MU-LD fails TU10; MU-F fails TU11; MU-S2 fails TQ1; MU-SR fails nothing (equivalent, as B said) |
| Browser delay/fail/idle/placement runs, both viewports | All valid and all as specified: exact placement + seed + Snap text with no "ready" overwrite, exact 1-line failed text, BPM/Snap correct, no leading space, 0 page errors |

The first browser run failed because Vite reloaded the page during a cold start; it ran clean after I added a warm-up.

The code-reviewer scored it 8/10 and found M1. Its other notes are minor or deliberate. Its architecture note is in the report as a signal for B, not a task: the status line now depends on matching text prefixes, which is what caused M1 and L1, and it suggests giving the status separate collection and action parts.

I did not run the full suite, `verify`, the build or a HEAD-server comparison; those belong to the gate and C. I haven't marked any C acceptance row as passed, and the round isn't done until B rules and the fix is re-dispatched.

The full report is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-237.md`, with evidence in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-237/`.
